document.bodyMarkdown:
This past week was Life Day (November 17, 2026). Life Day is a Wookie holiday that celebrates family, joy, harmony, and peace, featured in Star Wars: The Holiday Special, released on the same day. People celebrate it by wearing red robes, holding orb lights that symbolize family members who have returned to the Force, feasting, singing, and a modern tradition that seems to follow every major holiday: consumerism ((Looking at you, Ezra Legacy Lightsaber Set.) I mostly kid.)

However, the passing of this holiday made me reflect on our own personal holidays. Jedi, are there special days you set aside, the date of which cannot be found on any calendar, because it is inscribed on your heart? Personal observances of our own or others' history?

There are some typical answers to this question: anniversaries, birthdays, death days, apprenticeship dates, knighthood dates, and the like. These special days run the gamut of emotions one could feel when recalling them. (A word of warning, Jedi. Be wary of those holidays that run on the painful side, especially if there is no benefit of their recollection.)

I want to take an opportunity and share my special day.

August 21st 2022 – What I call The Best Day of My Life

That summer was hot and dry. It was ranked 7th in days (52) with temperatures above 100 degrees, and 2nd in days in a row (67) without measurable precipitation at the time. That day, we got a ton of rain, enough to break the drought. You would’ve thought it was the first time I’d seen rain because I raised all of the blinds and cracked the windows of the house. A dog who had not been feeling very well for a time had the energy to get out of his crate and mingle with my wife’s family (who had come down to visit) and us. The reason why my wife’s family came was to visit our newborn, who was a month old at the time. Some other things that happened that day: I reconnected with a coworker I hadn’t talked to in years and fell into an indie music phase for a time.

All in all, a pretty good day. Now that I described what happened, let me try to convey the significance, metaphor, and the emotions from that day.

You got a little of it, but the heat was oppressive. It was the first time in my career that I heard field employees (rightfully) being sent home to avoid heat-related illnesses. This period of time when the heat is especially hot is often referred to as the “Dog Days” of summer. The dog, who had not been doing well, eventually had to be put down a month later, but I often reflect on how good it was to see him with such energy that day. The song that popped into my head when we sadly had to put him down was “Dog Day’s Are Over” the meaning of which for most is about joy; but to me it also has a certain catharsis, especially in the line “leave all your love and your longing behind; you can’t carry it with you if you want to survive.” Sometimes we become attached to what was and is.

Jedi, it was a moment of rebirth for me. It was the beginning of a new era, where my responsibility was shifting from my pet dogs, to nurturing human life. That “Pet” era was 14 years, something that was very much a part of my daily life, and at the time, I thought my life would be unrecognizable without it. Up until that point, I understood that I was a father, but I had not yet realized it. Parenthood, like all new things, takes some time to get acclimated to.

The unstoppable, unlikely rain represented the unstoppable, unlikely change persistent in all of our lives. By “lives,” I mean not only the plural (all of us) but also the many lives we live in our single life. Jedi, all these events were interconnected. Sometimes change comes in a flood, and on that day it did.

I probably quote this teaching a lot, but Teaching Three says:

Not only should we be aware of these changes, but we should also do our best to recognize and celebrate them. Doing so creates a sacred moment in time for us to be grounded before continuing ever forward.

Sorry, I felt like I was rambling. It’s often difficult for me to convey emotion and feelings into words, but I say all that to ask: What are your special days, Jedi? Are there days you hold in your heart? What do we gain from remembering and celebrating those days? If you are comfortable with sharing, I invite you to do so.
